theory.heading: Match the tool to the purpose
theory.body: A safe tool decision begins before anything is used. First, identify the broad purpose of the task and consider whether the named tool is generally suited to that purpose. Recognising a tool does not automatically mean it is the correct choice or that you may use it. The task information provided by the teacher must guide the decision. Do not choose equipment because it is nearby, familiar or being used by another student. If the purpose of the task or tool is unclear, pause and ask before taking further action.

theory.heading: Check approval and condition
theory.body: Before tool use, check that you have teacher authorisation and that the current school SOP applies to the planned activity. Permission from another student is not enough. Without operating the tool, look for obvious signs of damage, loose parts, missing guards, unusual wear or anything else that appears unsafe. Do not test, adjust or attempt to repair equipment. Report the concern and wait for teacher direction. Current school SOPs and teacher instructions control all actual workshop activity.

theory.heading: Stay clear and resolve uncertainty
theory.body: Safe decisions also depend on what is happening nearby. Keep clear of active work, avoid distracting the person working and do not enter an authorised work area without direction. Observe whether your position, movement or materials could interfere with someone else. If any part of the tool, task, authorisation, condition or surrounding area is uncertain, stop and ask a precise question. Wait for confirmation before continuing. A useful check is: Does the tool match the broad purpose, am I authorised, does it appear undamaged and is the area clear?

questions.question: What should be identified first when making a tool decision?
choices: The intended broad purpose of the task
The colour of the tool
Which student used it last
Where the tool is stored
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Identifying the broad purpose helps determine whether the named tool may be generally suitable.
questions.retryFeedback: Review Match the tool to the purpose and focus on the first decision made before tool use.
questions.theoryAnchor: Match the tool to the purpose

questions.question: Why is recognising a tool not enough to begin using it?
choices: Recognised tools are never suitable
Teacher task information and authorisation are still required
Another student must use it first
Only damaged tools need approval
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Recognition does not replace teacher-provided task information or authorisation.
questions.retryFeedback: Return to Match the tool to the purpose and identify what recognition does not provide.
questions.theoryAnchor: Match the tool to the purpose

questions.question: Which is the weakest reason for selecting a tool?
choices: It matches the teacher-provided task information
Its broad purpose suits the task
It is nearby and familiar
The teacher has authorised its use
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Convenience and familiarity do not show that a tool is suitable or authorised.
questions.retryFeedback: Re-read Match the tool to the purpose and focus on reasons that should not guide selection.
questions.theoryAnchor: Match the tool to the purpose

questions.question: What must a student check before using a tool?
choices: Whether another student approves
Whether the activity can be finished quickly
Whether the tool is the newest one available
Whether teacher authorisation and the current SOP apply
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Teacher authorisation and the current SOP must apply before tool use.
questions.retryFeedback: Review Check approval and condition and identify the required approval and guidance.

questions.question: How should a student inspect equipment before use?
choices: Operate it briefly to test it
Look for obvious damage without operating it
Adjust any loose parts
Ask another student to repair it
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. The inspection is visual and should not involve operating, adjusting or repairing the equipment.
questions.retryFeedback: Return to Check approval and condition and focus on how the condition check is completed.

questions.question: What should a student do after noticing a loose or damaged part?
choices: Continue if the task is nearly finished
Attempt a simple repair
Report it and wait for teacher direction
Test whether the tool still works
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Possible damage must be reported, and the student should wait for teacher direction.
questions.retryFeedback: Re-read Check approval and condition and find the response to signs of damage.

questions.question: Which action shows appropriate behaviour near active work?
choices: Standing close to watch every movement
Entering the area to offer advice
Moving materials through the work area
Keeping clear and avoiding distractions
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Keeping clear and avoiding distractions reduces interference with active work.
questions.retryFeedback: Review Stay clear and resolve uncertainty and focus on behaviour around someone who is working.

questions.question: What should a student consider before moving near a work area?
choices: Whether their movement or materials could interfere with someone
Whether the tool looks interesting
Whether another student has finished talking
Whether they can move through quickly
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Students should consider how their position, movement and materials may affect others.
questions.retryFeedback: Return to Stay clear and resolve uncertainty and identify the surrounding-area observation.

questions.question: What is the best response when any part of a tool decision is uncertain?
choices: Choose the most familiar option
Continue slowly
Stop, ask a precise question and wait for confirmation
Copy another student
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. A precise question and teacher confirmation prevent decisions based on assumptions.
questions.retryFeedback: Re-read Stay clear and resolve uncertainty and focus on what happens when information is unclear.

questions.question: Which final check best supports a safe tool decision?
choices: The tool is nearby and another student has used it
The student remembers seeing the tool used before
The tool looks simple and the task seems easy
The tool matches the purpose, authorisation is confirmed, it appears undamaged and the area is clear
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. This check covers purpose, authorisation, visible condition and the surrounding area.
questions.retryFeedback: Review the final sentence of Stay clear and resolve uncertainty and identify all parts of the check.

written.prompt: Explain how a student should decide whether they are ready to use a named tool for a general teacher-provided task without describing any operating procedure.
written.sentenceStarter: The student should first identify ___. They must then check ___, inspect ___ and ___.
written.example: The student should first identify the broad purpose of the task. They must then check teacher authorisation and the current SOP, inspect the tool for obvious damage without operating it, and wait for confirmation if anything is unclear.
